chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from al-Qasim from Aban from Rabi' ibn al-Qasim said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the girl who has not yet reached menstruation, and pregnancy is feared for her. He said: Her womb is verified (cleared of pregnancy) by the one who sells her and the one who buys her, [through a period of] forty and four nights.
Thus it is clarified in this report and the first report that this obligation applies only if pregnancy is feared for her, and this occurs only when she is of the age at which she menstruates.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for verifying pregnancy in a young girl who has not yet menstruated?
ai.summary: In *Al-Istibsar*, Shaykh al-Tusi records this ruling from Imam al-Sadi' (AS) regarding *istibra'* (verification of pregnancy) for a pre-pubescent slave girl, specifying a forty-four-night period for both seller and buyer when pregnancy is feared. This establishes that the obligation arises not merely from age, but from the physiological likelihood of menstruation and conception, ensuring the buyer acquires a non-pregnant slave and the seller is released from liability.
